title: Stream checkpointing + keepalive protocol for incremental outputs & tool-call compatibility shim
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Long-running streaming responses (model -> client) sometimes produce large partial outputs and function/tool-call invocations where clients need to resume from a safe point after flaky mobile network disruptions or intermediary proxies that truncate connections. Current resume approaches rely on ad-hoc resume tokens and opaque chunk boundaries which create compatibility issues for downstream SDKs and for tool/function calling flows that expect atomic structured outputs.

Goal: Design and implement a lightweight checkpoint + keepalive protocol layered on top of SSE that: (1) provides resumable, idempotent incremental delivery for partial structured outputs and tool-call payloads, (2) offers a minimal wire-format compatible with existing SSE clients (no mandatory breaking changes), and (3) integrates with Redwood runtime routing to preserve latency and cost guarantees.
technical_design:
Overview: Introduce stable, short-lived checkpoint tokens (cp_id) emitted at safe boundaries in the stream. Each checkpoint marks a consistent state (complete JSON object or completed function-call invocation) and includes a sequence number and TTL. Between checkpoints, stream fragments carry fragment_ids and a checksum so partial fragments can be validated on reconnect. Additionally, introduce a keepalive heartbeat message (type: "hb") every 15s when idle to prevent intermediate proxies from closing connections and to help clients detect staleness faster.

Wire format (SSE-compatible):
- Keep existing 'data:' SSE lines for backward compatibility.
- Augment payloads with a small metadata envelope encoded as a single-line prefixed JSON, e.g.:
  data: {"t":"cp","cp_id":"cp_123","seq":42,"ttl":120}
  data: {"t":"fragment","frag_id":"f_456","cp_id":"cp_123","part":2,"checksum":"a1b2"}
  data: {"t":"hb"}  // keepalive
- Clients that do not parse cp/fragment fields will continue to assemble the stream as before; upgraded SDKs can use cp_id/frag_id to request resume ranges.

Resume semantics:
- On reconnect, client provides last-seen cp_id (or frag_id+offset) via an ephemeral query param (resume_cp=cp_123) or header (X-Resume-Cp).
- Server validates cp_id TTL and returns a brief handshake SSE response that replays any missing checkpoints/fragments, then switches to live streaming.
- If cp_id expired or unknown, server responds with a full re-send policy: either replay last N tokens up to a configurable cap or signal an unrecoverable restart.

Function/tool-call integrity:
- Tool-call invocations are emitted only at checkpoint boundaries (t:\"cp\" with additional field call:{...}). This ensures a resumed client cannot see a partial tool payload in isolation.
- If a tool-call requires streaming (e.g., incremental args), we batch until a safe checkpoint can be emitted, or we emit an explicit \"call-stream\" envelope that is considered atomic for resume semantics.

Runtime integration:
- Checkpoint generation is possible at the runtime kernel level where KV cache boundaries or completed JSON trees are detected. We will implement heuristics: end-of-sentence punctuation + closed structured-object boundary OR explicit model signal token (recommended).
- Store cp metadata in Redis with TTL ~ 2 minutes and sequence pointer to fragments in object store for replay.

Backward compatibility:
- No mandatory wire change for older clients. New behavior is additive metadata in the 'data:' SSE lines and optional resume handshake endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SSE stream emits checkpoint (t:"cp") entries at safe structured boundaries for 90% of standard prompt workloads
2) Clients can reconnect providing resume_cp and receive exact continuation without duplication for sequences < TTL
3) Tool/function-call envelopes are never partially delivered across a checkpoint boundary (unit tests + fuzzer coverage),
4) Heartbeat messages emitted every 15s during idle periods and configurable via route settings
5) E2E latency impact < 2% on 95th percentile long-tail requests when checkpoints enabled
tasks: Design: finalize envelope schema and minimal fields (Marco)
Runtime: implement checkpoint detector hook and cp emission (runtime team)
Store: metadata persistence and fragment replay API (infra)
Gateway: add X-Resume-Cp header handling and resume handshake path (api-gateway)
SDKs: add resume logic to Node/Python SDKs, with fallbacks for older clients (dx)
Tests: property tests for idempotency, chaos tests for mid-stream disconnect (qa)
Docs: migration guide and sample code for resume/connect patterns (docs)
Rollout: behind feature flag per-tenant, gradual 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 weeks
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Checkpoint emission increases CPU/IO churn. Mitigation: sample-based checkpointing and config knob to disable for low-cost routes.
Risk: Proxies may strip headers used for resume. Mitigation: resume_cp allowed as query param fallback and SDK will retry using both header and query param.
Risk: TTL expiry causes user-visible restart. Mitigation: surface explicit restart event in stream (t:"restart_notice") and provide client guidance for graceful recovery.
Risk: Malformed fragments cause replay mismatch. Mitigation: include fragment checksums and server-side verification before accepting resume requests.
testing_plan: Unit tests for envelope parsing, integration test suite that simulates flaky TCP and HTTP/1.1 proxy truncation, end-to-end test with function-call scenario where the call payload is emitted atomically at cp boundary, and a chaos run in staging with 5000 simulated mobile clients reconnecting intermittently.
rollout_plan: Create feature-flag 'stream-cps' in runtime. Enable internally for infra teams (week 1), opt-in for selected customers (week 2), gradual ramp via console toggle to 10% traffic (week 3), monitor metrics (resume_success_rate, cp_emit_rate, tail_latency), then 50%/100% if stable.

2026-03-07 Security (Jonah Reed): Header-based resume could be abused for replay; ensure cp tokens are cryptographically opaque and bound to connection/session.
